# The Method's Character and Affinities
  ¶1 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): Pragmatism represents a perfectly familiar attitude in philosophy, the empiricist attitude, but it represents it, AS IT SEEMS TO ME, both in a more radical and in a less objectionable form than it has ever yet assumed.
  ¶2 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): But the general triumph of that method would mean an enormous change in WHAT I CALLED IN MY LAST LECTURE the 'temperament' of philosophy.
  ¶2 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): Teachers of the ultra-rationalistic type would be frozen out, MUCH AS THE COURTIER TYPE IS FROZEN OUT IN REPUBLICS, AS THE ULTRAMONTANE TYPE OF PRIEST IS FROZEN OUT IN PROTESTANT LANDS.
  ¶3 UNCOVERED: You know how men have always hankered after unlawful magic, and you know what a great part, in magic, WORDS have always played.
  ¶3 UNCOVERED: If you have his name, or the formula of incantation that binds him, you can control the spirit, genie, afrite, or whatever the power may be.
  ¶3 UNCOVERED: Solomon knew the names of all the spirits, and having their names, he held them subject to his will.
  ¶3 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): SO the universe has always appeared to the natural mind as a kind of enigma, of which the key must be sought in the shape of some illuminating or power-bringing word or name.
  ¶8 UNCOVERED: So much for the pragmatic method!
  ¶8 UNCOVERED: You may say that I have been praising it rather than explaining it to you, but I shall presently explain it abundantly enough by showing how it works on some familiar problems.
  ¶8 UNCOVERED: I mean to give a whole lecture to the statement of that theory, after first paving the way, so I can be very brief now.
  ¶8 UNCOVERED: But brevity is hard to follow, so I ask for your redoubled attention for a quarter of an hour.
  ¶8 UNCOVERED: If much remains obscure, I hope to make it clearer in the later lectures.
